title: Lecturers: Turn Lecture Slides into Course Videos (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Turn Lecture Slides into Course Videos
bullets: For students who missed the session
slides.notes: You already have years of lecture decks. Turned into video, they can teach on their own, before class, for revision, or for an online cohort.

slides.title: Start with decks where video helps most
bullets: Pre-class content for weeks you want to flip
slides.notes: Don't start with your whole course. A good first project is one assessment explainer. Every student needs it, and it saves you answering the same emails.

slides.title: Split one lecture into short videos
bullets: Before: Week 3 Lecture: Cell Biology (48 slides)
What a cell membrane does (8 slides)
Worked example: osmosis in plant cells (9 slides)
slides.notes: A fifty-minute lecture rarely works as one fifty-minute video. Give each concept its own short video, so students can find the part they need later.

slides.title: Write speaker notes as narration
bullets: Before: "Osmosis - water moves high to low conc."
After: "Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane."
Short sentences suit voices and captions
slides.notes: Swap dot points for what you'd actually say to a student. Short sentences work better for voices and captions, so check how technical terms are pronounced.

slides.title: Preview, then add it to your LMS
bullets: Pick a voice and speaking speed
slides.notes: Choose a slightly slower speed for dense material, and watch the whole video with sound. Then download the MP4 and add it to your course yourself.

slides.title: Start with one lecture
bullets: On Pro, a.i. directs the video
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing each scene to your narration so a lecture lands like a produced explainer. Try one on Basic at powerpoint2vid.com.
